paragraphs: Apple is giving video podcasts a big-screen boost. The second iOS 27.3 developer beta, released Monday, adds video podcasts to the Apple TV app on more than 1 billion devices.

Even better, the company will let anyone with the Apple TV app — whether on an Apple product, a smart TV or another streaming device like a Roku — watch the video podcasts for free, with no Apple TV subscription required.

By all accounts, Apple squandered its early lead in the podcasting game. The iPod, the Apple device that revolutionized the music industry in the early 2000s, made it possible to carry audio around for easy listening, and clever third-party software made it simple to transfer so-called audioblogs to the digital music player. (Apple added podcasts to iTunes 4.9 in June 2005, a year after journalist Ben Hammersley proposed the term “podcasting” in an article in The Guardian).

In the following years, podcasts gained steam and became a dominant force in media — while Apple apparently lost interest. What started out as a platform for independent creators to distribute audio content morphed into an audio/video phenomenon embraced by mainstream media companies as an alternative to traditional broadcasting.

Now, Apple is renewing its focus on the platform — and trying to catch up with competitors like YouTube, Spotify, Netflix and Hulu. First, Apple added video to select podcasts in its Podcasts app in February. Now it’s super-sizing its ambitions by bringing the popular video podcasts to the Apple TV app, wherever you might find it.

“We want podcasts to be available wherever people want to enjoy them — the small screens, big screens,” Oliver Schusser, vice president of Apple Music and international content, told The New York Times in a story published Monday. “It’s really about discovery and helping the creators to reach a new audience. We didn’t approach this in a way that would financially benefit us.”

Apple calls out the new ability to stream video podcasts in the Apple TV welcome screen after updating to iOS 27.3 beta 2. “Your favorite video podcasts are here,” says the card. “Watch full episodes right in the Apple TV app, and pick up where you left off from Apple Podcasts.”

That could prove especially handy if you’re listening to a podcast on your iPhone and the hosts start discussing something visual. Rather than watching it on your phone’s small display, you could easily switch to your TV’s big screen.
